First, we factor the numerator:

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{\operatorname{tan}⁡\theta -\operatorname{tan}⁡\theta {sin}^{2}⁡\theta }{2\operatorname{sin}⁡\theta \operatorname{cos}⁡\theta } & =\frac{\operatorname{tan}⁡\theta (1-{sin}^{2}⁡\theta )}{2\operatorname{sin}⁡\theta \operatorname{cos}⁡\theta }\end{aligned}
$$

Next, we rewrite the numerator using $1-{sin}^{2}⁡\theta ={cos}^{2}⁡\theta $ and simplify:

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{\operatorname{tan}⁡\theta (1-{sin}^{2}⁡\theta )}{2\operatorname{sin}⁡\theta \operatorname{cos}⁡\theta } & =\frac{\operatorname{tan}⁡\theta {cos}^{2}⁡\theta }{2\operatorname{sin}⁡\theta \operatorname{cos}⁡\theta } \\  & =\frac{\operatorname{tan}⁡\theta \operatorname{cos}⁡\theta \cancel{\operatorname{cos}⁡\theta }}{2\operatorname{sin}⁡\theta \cancel{\operatorname{cos}⁡\theta }} \\  & =\frac{\operatorname{tan}⁡\theta \operatorname{cos}⁡\theta }{2\operatorname{sin}⁡\theta } \\  & =\operatorname{tan}⁡\theta \cdot \frac{\operatorname{cos}⁡\theta }{2\operatorname{sin}⁡\theta }\end{aligned}
$$

Then, we rewrite $\operatorname{tan}⁡\theta $ using its definition and simplify further:

$$
\begin{aligned}\operatorname{tan}⁡\theta \cdot \frac{\operatorname{cos}⁡\theta }{2\operatorname{sin}⁡\theta } & =\frac{\operatorname{sin}⁡\theta }{\operatorname{cos}⁡\theta }\cdot \frac{\operatorname{cos}⁡\theta }{2\operatorname{sin}⁡\theta } \\  & =\frac{\cancel{\operatorname{sin}⁡\theta }}{\operatorname{cos}⁡\theta }\cdot \frac{\operatorname{cos}⁡\theta }{2\cancel{\operatorname{sin}⁡\theta }} \\  & =\frac{1}{\operatorname{cos}⁡\theta }\cdot \frac{\operatorname{cos}⁡\theta }{2} \\  & =\frac{1}{\cancel{\operatorname{cos}⁡\theta }}\cdot \frac{\cancel{\operatorname{cos}⁡\theta }}{2} \\  & =\frac{1}{2}\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, we conclude that:

$$
\frac{\operatorname{tan}⁡\theta -\operatorname{tan}⁡\theta {sin}^{2}⁡\theta }{2\operatorname{sin}⁡\theta \operatorname{cos}⁡\theta }=\frac{1}{2}
$$
